name: Margherita pizza
summary: Homemade pizza dough topped with uncooked tomato sauce, torn mozzarella and fresh basil.
equipment: heavy baking tray or pizza stone
method: Heat the oven to its highest setting (240 to 250°C) with a heavy baking tray or pizza stone inside for 20 minutes.
Stretch each ball of pizza dough into a 28 to 30 cm round on a sheet of baking paper.
Spread each with half the pizza sauce, leaving a border, and scatter over the torn, well-drained mozzarella (two 125 g balls).
Slide each pizza, on its paper, onto the hot tray and bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the crust is puffed and charred in spots.
Drizzle with the olive oil and scatter with the basil leaves.
notes: One serving is one whole 28 to 30 cm pizza. Times assume the dough and sauce are already made.

name: Vegetable pizza
summary: Tomato and mozzarella pizza topped with red pepper, mushrooms, red onion and black olives.
equipment: heavy baking tray or pizza stone
method: Heat the oven to its highest setting (240 to 250°C) with a heavy baking tray or pizza stone inside for 20 minutes.
Stretch each ball of pizza dough into a 28 to 30 cm round on a sheet of baking paper.
Spread each with half the pizza sauce and scatter with the torn mozzarella, then the thinly sliced red pepper, mushrooms and red onion, and the halved black olives. Sprinkle with the oregano.
Slide each pizza, on its paper, onto the hot tray and bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the crust is puffed and charred in spots.
Drizzle with the olive oil to serve.
notes: A variant of Margherita pizza with vegetables added and a little less mozzarella. One serving is one whole 28 to 30 cm pizza. Times assume the dough and sauce are already made.

name: Chicken pizza
summary: Tomato and mozzarella pizza topped with pan-fried chicken, green pepper and red onion.
equipment: heavy baking tray or pizza stone
method: Heat the oven to its highest setting (240 to 250°C) with a heavy baking tray or pizza stone inside for 20 minutes.
Cut the chicken breast into thin strips, toss with the olive oil, paprika and salt and fry in a hot frying pan for 5 to 6 minutes until just cooked through.
Stretch each ball of pizza dough into a 28 to 30 cm round on a sheet of baking paper.
Spread each with half the pizza sauce, scatter with the torn mozzarella, then the chicken, sliced green pepper and red onion.
Slide each pizza, on its paper, onto the hot tray and bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the crust is puffed and charred in spots.
notes: A variant of Margherita pizza with chicken and vegetables added. One serving is one whole 28 to 30 cm pizza. Times assume the dough and sauce are already made.

name: Tuna pizza
summary: Tomato and mozzarella pizza topped with tinned tuna, red onion, capers and black olives.
equipment: heavy baking tray or pizza stone
method: Heat the oven to its highest setting (240 to 250°C) with a heavy baking tray or pizza stone inside for 20 minutes.
Stretch each ball of pizza dough into a 28 to 30 cm round on a sheet of baking paper.

Spread each with half the pizza sauce and scatter with the torn mozzarella, the drained tuna (one tin) in flakes, the thinly sliced red onion, the capers and the halved black olives. Sprinkle with the oregano.
Slide each pizza, on its paper, onto the hot tray and bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the crust is puffed and charred in spots.
notes: A variant of Margherita pizza with tuna and toppings added. Uses tuna in water, drained. One serving is one whole 28 to 30 cm pizza. Times assume the dough and sauce are already made.

name: Pepperoni pizza
summary: Tomato and mozzarella pizza topped with sliced pepperoni and oregano.
equipment: heavy baking tray or pizza stone
method: Heat the oven to its highest setting (240 to 250°C) with a heavy baking tray or pizza stone inside for 20 minutes.
Stretch each ball of pizza dough into a 28 to 30 cm round on a sheet of baking paper.
Spread each with half the pizza sauce, scatter with the grated mozzarella and lay the pepperoni slices over the top. Sprinkle with the oregano.
Slide each pizza, on its paper, onto the hot tray and bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the crust is puffed and charred in spots.
notes: A variant of Margherita pizza with pepperoni, using grated low-moisture mozzarella. One serving is one whole 28 to 30 cm pizza. Times assume the dough and sauce are already made.

name: Pitta pizza
summary: Quick pizzas on white pitta breads with pizza sauce, mozzarella and oregano.
method: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Put the pitta breads on a baking tray.
Spread each with the pizza sauce, scatter with the grated mozzarella and oregano, and add halved cherry tomatoes if you like.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the edges are crisp and the cheese is bubbling.
notes: A variant of Margherita pizza with pitta breads in place of the dough. One serving is two pitta pizzas.

name: Tortilla pizza
summary: A thin, crisp pizza on a large flour tortilla, crisped in a pan and finished under the grill.
method: Heat the grill to high. Crisp one large (25 cm) flour tortilla in a dry ovenproof frying pan over a medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes.
Spread with the pizza sauce, scatter with the grated mozzarella and the halved cherry tomatoes.
Put the pan under the grill for 3 to 4 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and the edges are crisp. Scatter with the basil.
notes: A variant of Margherita pizza with a tortilla in place of the dough.

name: Homemade calzone
summary: Folded pizza dough filled with tomato sauce, ricotta, mozzarella, ham and mushrooms.
equipment: heavy baking tray or pizza stone
method: Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan) with a heavy baking tray inside.
Stretch each ball of pizza dough into a 25 cm round on a sheet of baking paper. Spread the pizza sauce over one half of each, leaving a 2 cm border.
Top the sauced halves with spoonfuls of ricotta, the grated mozzarella, the torn ham, the sliced mushrooms, the oregano and black pepper.
Fold the plain half over, press and crimp the edges to seal, and cut a small steam hole in the top. Brush with the olive oil.
Slide onto the hot tray on the paper and bake for 15 to 18 minutes until puffed and deep golden. Rest for 3 minutes before cutting.
notes: One serving is one calzone. Times assume the dough and sauce are already made.

name: Cheese and onion quiche
summary: A blind-baked shortcrust case filled with slow-cooked onions, Cheddar and a creamy egg custard.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Roll out the shortcrust pastry and line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin; prick the base and chill for 15 minutes. Line with baking paper and baking beans and bake blind for 15 minutes, then remove the paper and beans and bake for 5 minutes more until pale golden. Lower the oven to 170°C (150°C fan).
Meanwhile melt the butter in a frying pan and cook the thinly sliced onions gently for 12 to 15 minutes until soft and golden. Leave to cool a little.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, double cream, a pinch of nutmeg, the salt and black pepper.

Scatter the onions and grated Cheddar into the pastry case and pour over the egg mixture. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until just set with a slight wobble in the middle. Cool for 15 minutes before cutting into 6.
notes: Uses one batch of the shortcrust pastry component; a 230 g ready-made sheet (shortcrust-pastry-raw) can replace it.

name: Spinach quiche
summary: A blind-baked shortcrust case filled with garlicky spinach, feta, Parmesan and a creamy egg custard.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Roll out the shortcrust pastry and line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin; prick the base and chill for 15 minutes. Line with baking paper and baking beans and bake blind for 15 minutes, then remove the paper and beans and bake for 5 minutes more until pale golden. Lower the oven to 170°C (150°C fan).
Meanwhile melt the butter in a large pan, add the garlic and the spinach and stir until wilted. Cool, squeeze out the liquid and chop roughly.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, double cream, a pinch of nutmeg and black pepper (the cheeses bring enough salt).

Spread the spinach in the pastry case, crumble over the feta and pour in the egg mixture. Scatter with the grated Parmesan and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until just set. Cool for 15 minutes before cutting into 6.
notes: A variant of cheese and onion quiche: spinach, feta and Parmesan replace the onions and Cheddar.

name: Chicken pie
summary: Chicken thigh and leek in a creamy thyme and mustard sauce under a puff pastry lid.
method: Cut the boneless chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces and season with the salt and black pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large pan and brown the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes, then lift out.

Melt the butter in the pan and cook the sliced leeks and garlic for 6 to 8 minutes until soft. Stir in the plain flour and thyme for 1 minute, then gradually stir in the stock cube dissolved in 300 ml boiling water, then the milk, to make a smooth sauce.
Return the chicken, add the mustard and simmer for 10 minutes. Leave the filling to cool.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spoon the filling into the pie dish, lay the puff pastry over, trim and crimp the edges, brush with beaten egg and cut a steam hole.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is risen and deep golden.
notes: Uses about 225 g of a ready-rolled puff pastry sheet for the lid; trimmings are not counted. Leek weight is trimmed weight.

name: Fish pie with pastry
summary: Cod, smoked haddock, prawns and peas in a parsley white sauce under a puff pastry lid.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cut the skinless cod and smoked haddock into large chunks and put them in the pie dish with the raw prawns and the frozen peas.
Stir the chopped parsley and lemon zest into the warm white sauce, pour it over the fish and mix gently.
Lay the puff pastry over, trim and crimp the edges, brush with beaten egg and cut a steam hole.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the filling is bubbling; the fish cooks in the oven.
notes: Hake or any firm white fish can replace the cod. Times assume the white sauce is made.

name: Vegetable pie
summary: A double-crust shortcrust pie of cauliflower, spinach, peas and onion bound with ricotta, egg, Parmesan and olives.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cut the cauliflower into small florets and boil for 4 minutes, then drain well. Heat the olive oil in a large pan, cook the chopped onion for 8 minutes, then add the spinach and stir until wilted. Leave to cool.
Mix the cauliflower, onion and spinach with the frozen peas, ricotta, eggs, grated Parmesan, sliced black olives, salt and black pepper.

Roll out two-thirds of the shortcrust pastry and line the pie dish. Spoon in the filling. Roll out the rest for a lid, lay it on top, seal and crimp the edges, brush with beaten egg and cut a few steam holes.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden. Cool for 15 minutes before cutting into 6.
notes: Uses one and a half batches of the shortcrust pastry component for the base and lid.

name: Ricotta savoury tart
summary: A shortcrust case filled with ricotta beaten with eggs, Parmesan, lemon and basil, dotted with cherry tomatoes.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Roll out the shortcrust pastry and line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin; prick the base and chill for 15 minutes. Line with baking paper and baking beans and bake blind for 15 minutes, then remove the paper and beans and bake for 5 minutes more until pale golden. Lower the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Beat the ricotta with the eggs, grated Parmesan, lemon zest, torn basil, salt and black pepper until smooth.
Pour into the pastry case, dot with the halved cherry tomatoes cut side up and drizzle with the olive oil.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until set and lightly golden. Cool for at least 20 minutes; good warm or at room temperature.

name: Sausage rolls
summary: Seasoned pork sausage meat with onion and thyme wrapped in puff pastry; makes 8.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Mix the sausage meat (skins removed) with the very finely chopped onion, the breadcrumbs, thyme and black pepper.

Cut the puff pastry sheet (320 g) in half lengthways. Lay half the filling along each strip in a long sausage shape, brush the far edge with beaten egg, fold the pastry over and press to seal. Cut each roll into 4.
Put on the tray, brush the tops with egg, sprinkle with sesame seeds if using and snip the tops with scissors. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until puffed, deep golden and cooked through.
notes: One serving is one large roll. The catalogue sausage is a generic pork sausage record; check your sausage meat label if it differs. Uncooked rolls freeze well.

name: Cheese pastry turnovers
summary: Puff pastry triangles filled with Cheddar, cream cheese, spring onion and mustard; makes 6.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Mix the grated Cheddar with the cream cheese, sliced spring onions, mustard and black pepper.
Cut the puff pastry sheet (320 g) into 6 squares. Spoon the filling onto one half of each, diagonally, brush the edges with beaten egg, fold into triangles and press the edges with a fork.
Brush the tops with egg and cut a small slit in each. Bake for 18 to 22 minutes until puffed and golden. Cool for 5 minutes, as the filling is very hot.

name: Spinach and feta filo pie
summary: Layers of crisp buttered filo around a filling of spinach, feta, egg, onion and dill.
method: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Wilt the spinach in a large pan in batches, cool, squeeze dry and chop.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the olive oil and soften the chopped onion and garlic for 8 minutes; cool. Mix with the spinach, the crumbled feta, eggs, chopped dill, a pinch of nutmeg and black pepper.

Melt the butter with the rest of the olive oil. Brush the baking dish, then layer half the filo pastry sheets, brushing each with the butter mixture. Spread in the filling and cover with the rest of the filo, brushing each sheet and scrunching the top ones.
Score the top into 6 and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until crisp and deep golden. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

name: Beef and potato pasties
summary: Shortcrust pasties filled with diced raw beef, potato, onion and carrot that cook together in the oven; makes 6.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Cut the beef into small 1 cm pieces, discarding any gristle. Peel and finely dice the potato, onion and carrot, and mix everything with the salt and black pepper.

Divide the shortcrust pastry into 6 and roll each piece into an 18 cm round. Pile the filling onto one half of each round, dot with the butter, brush the edge with beaten egg, fold over and crimp to seal. Brush the tops with egg and cut a small steam hole.
Bake for 20 minutes, then lower the oven to 170°C (150°C fan) and bake for 30 to 35 minutes more until golden and the filling is tender when tested with a skewer.
notes: Carrot stands in for swede, which is not in the catalogue. Uses two batches of the shortcrust pastry component.

name: Tomato and goat's cheese tart
summary: A puff pastry tart spread with olive tapenade and topped with sliced tomatoes, goat's cheese and thyme.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Unroll the puff pastry sheet on its paper onto a baking tray. Score a 2 cm border all round without cutting through, and prick the inside with a fork.
Spread the tapenade inside the border, lay over the thinly sliced tomatoes, overlapping, and crumble over the goat's cheese. Sprinkle with the thyme and black pepper and drizzle with the olive oil.
Brush the border with beaten egg and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is puffed and golden underneath.
Cool for 5 minutes, then cut into 4.
notes: Uses the olive tapenade component; basil pesto works too.

name: Spiced lamb flatbreads
summary: Thin pizza-dough flatbreads baked with spiced lamb mince, pepper and tomato, finished with parsley, lemon and yogurt garlic sauce.
equipment: heavy baking tray or pizza stone
method: Heat the oven to its highest setting (240 to 250°C) with 2 heavy baking trays inside.
Mix the raw lamb mince with the very finely chopped onion and red pepper, the tomato paste, grated garlic, cumin, paprika, chilli flakes and salt.

Divide each ball of pizza dough in half and stretch or roll each piece very thinly into an oval about 30 cm long on baking paper. Spread a quarter of the lamb mixture thinly over each, right to the edges.
Slide onto the hot trays on their paper and bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the edges are crisp and the lamb is cooked.
Scatter with the chopped parsley, squeeze over the lemon juice and drizzle with the yogurt garlic sauce. Roll up or cut into strips to eat.
notes: Makes 4 thin flatbreads; one serving is one flatbread. Times assume the dough and sauce are already made.
